query: Casting is the predominant fabrication method for high-entropy alloys, but solidification-related porosity and microstructural nonuniformity can cause heterogeneous properties. Studies of other high-entropy-alloy compositions have reported high hardness and notable compressive performance, yet these findings do not establish how to improve CoCrFeNiTi; moreover, some investigated alloys were brittle at 25 °C and displayed only limited plastic deformation at 600 °C. For equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a simple crystal structure, favorable plasticity and machinability, but low hardness and load-bearing capability, what single intervention could improve hardness and mechanical performance while preserving those favorable characteristics and clarifying the relationship between microstructure and deformation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, a quantitative prediction relative to the unmodified alloy, the processing and testing boundaries within which it should apply, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled microstructural and mechanical experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Ti to CoCrFeNi will improve its hardness and mechanical performance while preserving favorable plasticity and machinability.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNi with a simple crystal structure
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a single-phase FCC structure or a dual-phase structure of FCC and Laves
generation.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and lattice distortion caused by the addition of Ti
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved hardness and mechanical performance, including increased ultimate tensile strength and hardness, while maintaining favorable plasticity and machinability
generation.boundary: Ti content up to 1.5 molar ratio
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of the improvement in mechanical properties and the optimal Ti content for the best balance of properties

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare CoCrFeNi alloys with varying Ti contents (0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 molar ratio) using an electrochemical process and vacuum hot pressing sintering
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Ti does not result in improved hardness and mechanical performance, or if the optimal Ti content is outside the predicted boundary, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: The hardness and elastic modulus of the TiZrNbTaMox high-entropy alloy increase linearly with the concentration of the Mo element (0 ≤ x ≤ 20), while the ductility of the alloy decreases. When the concentration of the Mo element is 20%, the alloy has good corrosion resistance [,]. However, the influence of temperature and strain rate on the properties of the TiNbTaZrMo high-entropy alloy is still limited. Thus, this research focuses on an HEA with Ti, Nb, Ta, Zr, and Mo, among which Ti, Nb, Ta, and Zr all have the function of improving the plasticity and ductility of the HEA. In addition, Ti and Zr are isomorphic in the solid state at room temperature, and Nb and Ta are also isomorphic; they have infinite compatibility and can be well fused. Mo can improve the hardness of HEAs. In order to maintain the hardness of the HEA while improving the plasticity, a Ti68Nb7Ta3Zr4Mo18 (at.%) HEA was chosen and simulated to obtain the effects of temperature, strain rate, and grain size on the mechanical properties of the Ti68Nb7Ta3Zr4Mo18 HEA. A series of five-element CoCrFeNi-Nbx (x = 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 wt%) high-entropy alloys were prepared using high-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering methods. Then, the effects of doping with Nb elements on the organization and properties of the CoCrFeNi HEAs were systematically investigated by tensile testing, hardness testing, and examining their micro-morphologies. The results show that with the addition of the Nb element, the lattice distortion of the alloy due to the large size of the Nb atoms causes the microstructure of CoCrFeNi HEAs to change from a single-phase FCC structure to a dual-phase structure of FCC and Laves. With the increase in the Nb content, the increase in the volume fraction of the hard and brittle Laves phase leads to the enhancement of the HEA’s tensile strength, yield strength, and hardness, and a decrease in plasticity. The Nb5 alloy showed the most excellent comprehensive performance, with a tensile strength, yield strength, and plasticity of 879.1 MPa, 491.8 MPa, and 39.8%, respectively, and all the properties were improved compared with those of the HEAs obtained by the arc melting method. The CoCrFeNi system is one of the most important high entropy alloys (HEAs) systems. By adding and adjusting the alloy element components and using different synthesis methods, different phases, organization and microstructure can be obtained, thus improving their properties. In this study, CoCrFeNiTix HEAs with various Ti contents (x in molar ratio, x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) were fabricated by an electrochemical process by virtue of different oxides. The impacts of different Ti contents on the structure, distribution of elements, mechanical properties and corrosion behavior were researched using XRD, EDX and other testing methods. The bulk CoCrFeNiTix (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) HEAs could be obtained through vacuum hot pressing sintering process (VHPS), which had a single-phase FCC structure. The results of the study showed that the bulk CoCrFeNiTix exhibited superior ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and hardness, with the UTS of CoCrFeNiTi as high as 783 MPa and the hardness of CoCrFeNiTi1.5 reaching 669 HV.
